text:
Logan Cooley scored three times for Utah and still lost. Montreal erased a two-goal deficit, got the first NHL goal from Adam Engstrom (a defenseman taken 92nd overall in 2022 who had spent last season with the Laval Rocket), and won 5-4 when Cole Caufield scored 30 seconds into overtime. Cooley, the third pick in 2022, had scored on a backhand, then twice on the power play, to put UTA up 3-2 in the second.

The game was not as even as the score. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored MTL 4.60 to 3.64, and our simulation of every shot says the Canadiens deserved to win 64 percent of the time. They outshot Utah 35 to 20 and took control in the third period, out-chancing the Mammoth 1.86 to 0.91. Even strength was dead level at 2.01 apiece, so the gap came from special teams. UTA scored on three of five power plays, but MTL generated 2.48 expected goals on its four, against 1.52 for Utah, and converted once. Arber Xhekaj's slap shot to tie it 2-2 late in the first came from a 2 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night.

Nick Suzuki, who had a goal and two assists, was named first star, with Lane Hutson logging 27 minutes and adding two assists. The facts we have don't include standings or streaks, so all we can say is that Montreal took the extra point in a game it trailed 4-3 after Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal, and that Utah, after a three-goal night from its young center, leaves with one point instead of two.
